result.question: Will the US and China agree to or announce another extension of the Busan trade truce before Jan 11, 2027?
result.rules:
If the US and China agree to or announce another extension of the Busan trade truce before Jan 11, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.

Another extension means that, after Issuance, both governments announce that the Busan trade truce will continue past Jan 10, 2027. It must cover China's suspension of its additional 24% tariff on US goods and the US suspension of port fees on China-linked ships, which are now due to expire on Jan 10, 2027, or be a statement that the truce as a whole is extended. A longer-lasting trade arrangement that replaces them also qualifies.

A joint statement qualifies, as do separate official statements or notices from each government. An announcement by one government qualifies only if the other government also confirms it, and counts from the date of that confirmation. An extension announced by only one government, an extension of other measures only, and an agreement on purchases or tariff cuts that leaves those suspensions to expire do NOT qualify. Extensions announced before Issuance, including the two-month extension to Jan 10, 2027, do NOT count.

An agreement or announcement qualifies if it involves any of the following:

Formal signing of treaties
Parliamentary approval with binding effect
Official ratification
Formal commitment by the head of state/government with constitutional authority
Official statements by authorized ministers
Official press releases
Formal declarations during government proceedings
Official statements to international bodies

Phased implementation announcements and multi-party agreements where the country is a signatory also qualify.

The following do NOT qualify:

Preliminary discussions
Conditional agreements contingent on circumstances
Opposition party statements
Leaked documents
Think-tank recommendations
General aspirations without specific commitment
Draft legislation without approval
Regional actions (unless specified)
Retraction of previously announced commitments
